definitions.explanation: The medical or formal term for the act of urinating. Used in healthcare settings, medical literature, and formal descriptions of bodily functions.

examples.japanese: {排尿|はいにょう}の{回数|かいすう}が{増|ふ}えた。
examples.english: The frequency of urination has increased.

examples.japanese: {排尿|はいにょう}{時|じ}に{痛|いた}みがある{場合|ばあい}は{受診|じゅしん}してください。
examples.english: If you have pain during urination, please see a doctor.

examples.japanese: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}の{排尿|はいにょう}{障害|しょうがい}は{生活|せいかつ}の{質|しつ}に{大|おお}きく{影響|えいきょう}するため、{早|はや}めに{専門医|せんもんい}に{相談|そうだん}することが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: Urinary disorders in the elderly greatly affect quality of life, so it is important to consult a specialist early.

notes:
Composed of {排|はい} (expel, discharge) and {尿|にょう} (urine). A formal, medical term — in everyday conversation, Japanese speakers use トイレに{行|い}く (to go to the bathroom) or {小|しょう}をする (to urinate, colloquial). {排尿|はいにょう} appears on medical questionnaires, in health articles, and in clinical discussions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {排尿|はいにょう}{障害|しょうがい}: urinary disorder
- {排尿|はいにょう}{困難|こんなん}: difficulty urinating
- {排尿|はいにょう}{回数|かいすう}: urination frequency
- {排尿|はいにょう}{痛|つう}: pain during urination
- {排尿|はいにょう}を{促|うなが}す: to promote urination

RELATED WORDS:
- {排便|はいべん}: defecation — the corresponding term for bowel movements
- {頻尿|ひんにょう}: frequent urination — a common urological complaint
- {尿|にょう}: urine — the substance itself
